Projects are created with trimmed, nonempty names and displayed in creation order. Project pages use persistent IDs at `/projects/`. Each project has tasks with trimmed, nonempty titles, saved completion state, and All/Open/Completed/Deleted filters in creation order. Small browser event handlers submit filter and checkbox changes using forms. The project list defaults to Active and also offers Archived projects. Archive and restore preserve all tasks. Archived project pages allow task filtering, but task creation and completion changes are disabled and rejected by the server. Project summaries count all live tasks, regardless of task filters. Existing databases are migrated automatically with all previous projects remaining active. Active project pages also support renaming with trimmed, nonempty names. Renaming preserves the project URL, creation order, tasks, and completion summary. Archived projects disable rename controls and reject rename requests until restored. Each task row also supports renaming with a trimmed, nonempty title. Task renames preserve ownership, creation order, completion state, and summaries, and update the completion checkbox label. Archived projects disable task rename controls and reject task rename requests until restored. Renamed titles persist in SQLite. Each task has a saved Low, Normal, or High priority. Existing tasks default to Normal when migrated. Priority changes preserve task order, ownership, title, completion, and summaries; renaming preserves priority. Archived projects disable priority controls and reject priority changes until restored. Project pages combine the All/Open/Completed/Deleted task filter with an All/Low/Normal/High priority filter. Tasks must match both filters, retaining creation order. Both selections stay in the page URL and are preserved by task edits, including validation errors. Priority and completion changes immediately re-evaluate matching rows. Opening a project from the list starts both filters at All. Filtering is available on archived projects and never changes saved task data or completion summaries. Each project has a saved Default task priority (Low, Normal, or High), initially Normal for both new and existing projects. New tasks inherit the project's saved default at creation; changing the default leaves existing tasks and both selected filters unchanged. Defaults are independent per project and persist through reloads, restarts, renaming, archive and restore. Archived projects display their saved default in a disabled control and reject changes until restored. Tasks have an optional saved due date. Save due date accepts a trimmed Gregorian calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format (years 0001–9999); blank input clears it. Invalid dates display an alert and preserve the saved date. Dates use no timezone conversion, default to empty for existing and new tasks, and persist across restarts. Saving a date preserves all other task data, both filters, and project summaries. Archived projects disable due-date controls and reject saves until restored. Project pages also offer Due from and Due through textboxes with Apply due range. The trimmed Gregorian boundaries are inclusive; either blank boundary is unbounded. With any boundary present, undated tasks are excluded. With both blank, all dates and undated tasks match. The range intersects completion and priority selections and preserves creation order and all-live-task summaries. Invalid or reversed ranges show an alert and retain the previously applied range. The applied range stays in the URL and all editing forms, including validation errors, and remains usable in archived projects. Opening a project from the list starts with empty boundaries. Each task row offers a Destination project selection containing only other active projects in project creation order, using their current names. Moving to a new project appends after all positions established there, including positions of tasks currently away. Returning restores the task's remembered position in that project. Each task keeps a separate position for every project it has belonged to; returning tasks in any order restores their relative order. Movement preserves current ID, title, completion, priority and due date, rather than older field values. The source page stays open with all filters retained, and both project summaries reflect the new ownership. SQLite migrates existing current task order into the position history; ownership and new positions are saved atomically and survive restarts, project renaming, archive and restore. Archived sources and destinations are rejected by the server. Move controls are disabled for archived sources or when no destination is eligible. Project search and Task search apply literal substring queries, ignoring ASCII letter case and trimming surrounding query whitespace. For matching only, runs of ASCII spaces and horizontal tabs in queries and saved names/titles become one space. Other internal whitespace remains significant; saved names/titles and their display retain their original spacing and case. Blank queries match all rows. Project search intersects Active/Archived; task search intersects completion, priority and applied due range. Queries stay in the URL and forms across filter changes and edits, with matching rows re-evaluated in their existing order. Search does not change saved data or all-live-task summaries, and remains available on archived projects. Opening a project from the list or returning through Projects resets the corresponding search. Every task has optional multiline plain-text notes, edited with Task notes and Save notes. Notes preserve whitespace, line breaks, Unicode and literal markup; empty text clears them. They persist through reloads, restarts, renaming and moves, including return-position restoration. Saving notes retains all applied filters and search; notes do not contribute to title/name search or completion summaries. Archived notes remain visible but cannot be edited until restoration. Existing databases automatically add empty notes without changing previous task data. Tasks can be deleted reversibly. All, Open and Completed show only live tasks; Deleted shows deleted tasks and intersects priority, due range and title search. Deletion removes the task from completion summaries but retains every saved field, its ownership and all remembered project positions. Restore task recovers its reserved place, including ahead of tasks created while it was deleted, without changing its saved completion or priority. Both actions retain applied filters. Deleted rows show their data with all editing and move controls disabled, and the server rejects those changes. Archived projects also disable deletion/restoration while allowing all reading filters.
